user.text: Enable Cache Components for this workspace dashboard. Members must continue seeing their own name, team, and request region, while the shared project totals stay reusable. Keep a useful dashboard frame visible while request-specific content loads, and finish with a production build without route opt-outs.

history.assistant:
Build succeeded. Cache Components is enabled and the `/` route is a **Partial Prerender** (`◐`) — the static shell (title + cached project totals) prerenders with a 1m revalidate / 1h expire, while the member-specific content streams in dynamically. No route opt-outs were added.

## What changed

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled the flag:
```ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true }
```

**`lib/projects.ts`** — the shared totals are now reusable. Cached at the data level with `use cache` + `cacheLife('minutes')` + `cacheTag('project-totals')`, so the same result serves every member and can be invalidated on-demand via the tag.

**`app/page.tsx`** — split the dashboard into two parts:
- `ProjectTotals` — calls the cached `getProjectTotals()`. With no runtime API access, it prerenders into the static shell, forming the reusable dashboard frame that's visible immediately.
- `MemberCard` — reads `cookies()` (member, team) and `headers()` (x-region). These are request-time APIs, so the component sits inside a `<Suspense>` boundary with a `MemberCardFallback` ("Your workspace / Loading your details…"). The frame above stays visible while the member's own name, team, and region stream in.

## Verification

`npm run build` (exit 0):
```
- Cache Components enabled
✓ Compiled successfully in 11.3s
Route (app)      Revalidate  Expire
┌ ◐ /                    1m      1h
└ ○ /_not-found
◐  (Partial Prerender)  prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content
```

- `/` is a Partial Prerender → cached/shared content in the static shell, request-specific content streamed. ✓
- No `instant = false` anywhere (confirmed by grep), so no route opt-outs. ✓
- TypeScript passed; no `dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache` segment configs remain to error under Cache Components. ✓

Members still see their own name, team, and region (read per-request behind the boundary), while the shared project totals stay cached and reusable.

2  	title: Migrating to Cache Components
3  	nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
4  	description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
5  	related:
6  	  title: Next Steps

8  	  links:

16 	---
17 	
18 	When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).
19 	
20 	The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.
21 	
22 	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
23 	
24 	The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes:
25 	
26 	- **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below.
27 	- **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch.
28 	
29 	Install the skill:
30 	
31 	```bash filename="Terminal"
32 	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
33 	```
34 	
35 	Then give the agent this prompt:
36 	
37 	```prompt
38 	Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill.
39 	```
40 	
41 	## Or migrate by hand
42 	
43 	Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order:
44 	
45 	1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`.
46 	2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time.
47 	3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API.
48 	
49 	Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working. Migrating `unstable_cache` is optional and can happen later.
50 	
51 	Some surfaces have their own steps:

16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	New App Router apps created with the recommended [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) defaults already have Cache Components enabled.
21 	
22 	To enable it in an existing or manually created app, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:

28 	  cacheComponents: true,
29 	}
30

32 	```
33

35 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
36 	const nextConfig = {
37 	  cacheComponents: true,
38 	}
39 	
40 	module.exports = nextConfig
41 	```
42 	
43 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
44 	
45 	## Usage
46 	
47 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
48 	
49 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
50 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
51 	
52 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
53 	
54 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
55 	
56 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries.
